reach.rationale: Zero experimental, preview or RC APIs; the newest thing is the v22 @Service() decorator (5 months old, stable at launch) plus a couple of 2025-era stable SSR APIs. This sits between the 'only long-stable' and 'recently-stable in central places' anchors, leaning conservative.

justification.rationale: Every newish API buys something concrete a stable alternative couldn't (404 status, event replay, host validation), and the app consistently picks stable primitives over flashier experimental options even when v22 offered them.

findings.issue: @Service() is a very new API (stable since Angular v22, June 2026). Stable and CLI-default, so low risk, but it is the only thing in the codebase a v21-era reader wouldn't recognize.
findings.suggestion: Fine to keep; if the team wants maximum familiarity, the equivalent @Injectable({providedIn: 'root'}) is a one-line change.

findings.issue: @angular/forms is declared as a dependency but never imported anywhere in src/ — dead dependency (the app has no forms, experimental Signal Forms or otherwise).
findings.suggestion: Remove @angular/forms from dependencies to keep the bundle graph and dependency list honest.

summary: The app is deliberately conservative: zero experimental, preview, RC or canary APIs, and it steers clear of v22's genuinely experimental offerings (debounced(), injectAsync(), WebMCP, @boundary). The newest surface is the stable-since-June-2026 @Service() decorator, used once in the central data service where it's trivially swappable, plus 2025-era stable SSR/hydration APIs, each with a concrete justification. Risk of breaking-change exposure is minimal.
